To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) was synthesized by the dummy molecular imprinting method and the hybrid organic-inorganic material technique and that the prepared MIP was successfully used to extract fluoroquinolone antibiotics from fish samples.

we successfully synthesised an MI-MAA(APTS) sorbent for the selective isolation of fluoroquinone antibiotics in tilapia samples, and this sorbent exhibited good selectivity and recovery, as well as high mechanical strength.

the novel molecularly imprint organic-inorganic hybrid polymers (MI-MAAs/APTS) were synthesised and used for the first time as a sorbents in solid-phase extraction (SPE), and the presented MI-MAAs/APTs-SPE-HPLCM method can be applied to the determination and isolation of ofloxacin, lomefloxin, and ciprofloxacine in complex fish samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of a novel MI-MAA/ATPS sorbent and the application of this sorbent in a solid-phase extraction procedure for the selective isolation of OFL, L OM, and CIP in tilapia samples.
the synthesis of a novel molecular imprinting material and the development of a novel molecular recognition method for the selective isolation of FQs from complex fish samples.
the development of a novel MI-MAA(APTS)-SPE-HPLC technique for the determination of FQs in complex tilapia samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the MI-MAA/ APTS sorbent was successfully prepared, which could be used to selectively isolate FQs from complex fish samples and could be potentially applied in the determination of FQs in complex samples.
the MI-MAA/ APTS sorbent is a promising sorbent for the selective isolation of OFL, L OM, and C IP in fish samples.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MI-MAA/ATPS sorbent was successfully prepared and applied in SPE-HPLC method for the selective extraction of FQs in tilapia samples.
the MI-MAA/ APTS-SPE-HPL C method is simple and rapid, which is suitable for routine monitoring of OFL, L OM, and CIP in fish samples.
the novel MI-MAA/ APTS sorbent was developed by combining the molecular imprinting technique with an organic-inorganic material technique and exhibited high selectivity and affinity to the FQs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we developed a novel molecularly printed organic-inorganic hybrid sorbent for the selective isolation of fluoroquinones (FQ) in tilapia, which is a promising method for the determination of FQs in complex fish samples.
the MI-MAA(APTS) sorbent is an efficient, selective, and stable sorbent that can be used for the isolation of fluoroquinones from fish samples.
a molecularly imprinted polymer with high mechanical strength and good selectivity can be prepared by using a dummy molecular imprint technique and an organic–inorganic hybrid material technique.
